text:
PARIS — Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen said she was wrong to have opposed same-sex marriage and dual citizenship earlier in her career.
“One can evolve in politics, there is nothing to be ashamed of, one just has to explain why they have changed their mind,” Le Pen, the front-runner to win next year’s presidential race, said in an interview broadcast on Sunday by television channel LCP.
After initially opposing same-sex marriage when it was legalized in France in 2013, Le Pen said during her presidential campaign in 2022 that she would not touch the historic law.
She said in the interview, which was conducted by a high school student with a popular political platform on social media, that when the bill was passed she feared legalizing same-sex marriage would lead to the widespread use of surrogacy, which is not permitted in France and which Le Pen still opposes.
Le Pen has a history of moderating or backtracking on controversial positions to widen her base of support and push her populist party into the political mainstream. After her crushing defeat to current President Emmanuel Macron in the 2017 presidential election, Le Pen abandoned her calls for France to leave the EU — though her critics contend her plans for Brussels would wreak havoc on the bloc or lead to France’s ouster.
Asked during the interview about her other regrets, Le Pen evoked her previous opposition to dual citizenship. During parliamentary elections in 2024 , Le Pen’s party, the National Rally, stoked controversy with a proposal to ban dual nationals from holding certain positions in government.
“For a long time, I proposed banning dual citizenship … I think I made a mistake,” she said. “I gave those with dual citizenship the impression that I had some kind of suspicion regarding their love or commitment to France. I have changed my mind on that position, and I think I did the right thing.”
